title: The bulk change count does not count the cores that change with their parts
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Create two active parts for this test, part A and part B, each with a Core Charge above $0, so each has a core.
  • Give parts A and B part numbers that start with the same text, so one search lists both.
  • Start on the Inventory page (Parts in the top bar, then Inventory in the left menu), on the Active tab.
custom_steps:
1. Type the shared start of the part numbers in the Search box.
  2. Click the three-dot actions button (⋮) in the toolbar, to the left of New Inventory Part.
  3. Click Deactivate parts.
  4. Click the part A row.
  5. Click the part B row.
  6. Click Deactivate on the dark bar.
  7. Click Deactivate in the confirmation.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Parts A and B are listed, each with its core charge in the Core column and no separate core row.

Step 2:

  • The menu opens.

Step 3:

  • Bulk mode turns on.

Step 4:

  • The bar reads 1 selected.

Step 5:

  • The bar reads 2 selected.

Step 6:

  • The confirmation reads "2 parts selected."

Step 7:

  • Parts A and B leave the Active tab without a page reload.
  • A green message reads "2 parts updated.": the 2 ticked parts are counted and their 2 cores are not (2, not 2 + 2 = 4).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 33 (23 Oct 2026, owner Chris Ward), read 27 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10823 (Story 10, Confirming and Recording a Status Change)

  • S10-R12: “After a bulk change, the system shows how many parts changed and how many failed.”
  • S10-R12a: “The counts include only the parts the user selected. A core that changes with its part is not counted, so changing 2 parts that both have a core reads "2 parts updated."”
  • User Feedback Summary: “Bulk change, every part changed | "{n} parts updated." ("1 part updated." for one) | Success toast, fades on its own”

From: Jira tickets and comments under epic SV-10647 (saved in sources/jira-2026-10-27/ALL-TICKETS-2026-10-27.md), read 27 Oct 2026

  • SV-10823 acceptance criteria: “Given two parts that both have a core, when they are deactivated in bulk, then the message reads "2 parts updated."”
